default.label: Earlier years: arrears and updated returns
On the CA side: firms, LLPs, companies, HUFs and traders with books

params.name: rules

default.law: Rule 12, Income-tax Rules 1962; the ITR forms notified for AY 2026-27
default.plain: Picks ITR-1, ITR-2, ITR-3 or ITR-4 from what the return holds: residence, total income, houses, capital gains, farm income, directorship, unlisted shares, foreign assets, losses carried, and presumptive business income. The first reason that applies is shown to the person.

default.law: s.139(1) as amended by the Finance Act 2026; s.139(4) belated; s.139(5) revised; s.139(8A) updated
default.plain: The due date for the form (non-business 31 July; ITR-3 / ITR-4 without audit 31 August; audit 31 October - and always for a company (ITR-6); transfer pricing 30 November), any date CBDT extended for that year by circular (AY 2026-27: Circular 07/2026 - audit cases 21 November, audit report 21 October), and what a return filed on a given day is: on time, belated, revised (free to 31 December, then to 31 March with the s.234I fee) or updated.
The fee on a return revised after 31 December of the assessment year: 1,000 when total income is up to five lakh, 5,000 otherwise.

default.law: First Schedule, Part I (age bands for the old-regime slabs); s.80TTB; s.207(2)
default.plain: Below 60, 60 to 80, or 80 and above, on the last day of the previous year - decides the old-regime basic exemption, 80TTB and freedom from advance tax.

default.law: ss.15-17; s.16(ia) standard deduction; s.16(iii) professional tax; s.10 exemptions; s.115BAC(2)
default.plain: Income from salary: gross salary less exempt allowances (only those the new regime keeps), the standard deduction for the regime, and professional tax (old regime).
default.gaps: Relief u/s 89 for arrears (Form 10E) is not worked out.

default.plain: HRA exempt in the old regime: the least of HRA received, rent paid less 10% of salary, and 50% (metro) or 40% of salary.

default.law: ss.22-24; s.23(2) self-occupied; s.24(a) 30%; s.24(b) interest; s.115BAC(2)
default.plain: One house: annual value (rent less municipal tax; nil when self-occupied), 30% standard deduction, and interest on the loan - capped for a self-occupied house in the old regime, not allowed for one in the new regime.
default.gaps: Co-ownership share is taken as 100%; pre-construction interest (1/5 for 5 years) is not split out.

default.plain: All houses together; a loss from house property set off against other heads only up to the cap, and not at all in the new regime.

default.law: s.71 (set-off of a loss in the same year)
default.plain: Where the house loss goes this year: against salary first, then other sources, up to the cap; the rest is carried forward.
default.gaps: Set-off against business income is not yet done; carried-forward losses (Schedule CFL) are not built.

default.plain: Family pension after its deduction: one-third, up to the regime's cap.

default.law: s.44AD (business), s.44ADA (profession), with their turnover / receipts limits
default.plain: Presumptive income: 44ADA 50% of receipts; 44AD 6% of bank / digital turnover and 8% of cash - or more, if the person declares more. The limit rises when cash is at most 5% of receipts. Over the limit the presumptive basis is closed and the return needs books (ITR-3).
default.gaps: 44AE (goods carriages) is not built. A lower income than presumptive with books and audit is the CA side's work.

default.plain: Each deduction capped by its own section and by the overall 80CCE cap for 80C + 80CCC + 80CCD(1); in the new regime only the employer's NPS contribution 80CCD(2) (and 80CCH) is allowed.
default.gaps: 80G takes the amount as eligible (no 50% / qualifying-limit split); 80EE and 80EEA cannot both be claimed - the person is warned only in the rule book for now.

default.plain: Rent paid by an individual with no HRA from an employer, old regime: the least of 5,000 a month, 25% of total income and rent less 10% of total income - total income here being what is left after every other deduction.

default.law: First Schedule Part I (Finance Act 2025); s.115BAC(1A) new slabs; ss.111A, 112A, 112; s.87A rebate and marginal relief; surcharge and marginal relief; 4% health and education cess
default.plain: Tax at the regime's slabs on normal income, special rates on capital gains (111A, 112A above its exemption, 112), the 87A rebate with its marginal relief in the new regime, surcharge with marginal relief, then cess.
Which regime costs less; the old regime is open only to a return filed by the due date (and, with business income, a Form 10-IEA by then).
Total income: gross total income less deductions, rounded to the nearest ten rupees.

default.law: Finance Act 2025 (rates for AY 2026-27); the Act's caps and limits
default.plain: Every figure the calculation uses for the year: slabs, rebate, surcharge bands, cess, standard deduction, caps, rates and the ITR-1 limits. The Tax rules screen fetches and applies each new year's.

default.law: ss.234A, 234B, 234C; Rule 119A (amounts rounded down to 100); s.211(1)(b) single instalment for 44AD / 44ADA
default.plain: Interest for filing late (234A), for advance tax short of 90% (234B) and for each instalment short (234C), counted in months as the Act counts them.
A resident senior citizen with no business or profession income owes no advance tax - so no 234B / 234C.

default.law: Challan 280 minor heads (100 advance tax, 300 self-assessment, 400 regular assessment)
default.plain: Whether a challan is advance tax or self-assessment tax: by its minor head, and anything paid after the year ended is self-assessment.
The late fee on a return filed after the due date - lower when total income is up to five lakh.
Tax payable or refund: tax with interest and fee, less TDS, TCS and tax paid.

default.law: s.87A (a resident individual only); First Schedule Part I
default.plain: An HUF is taxed at the same slabs as an individual below 60, in either regime, but gets no 87A rebate and no marginal relief under it: 12 lakh of income pays tax plus cess.

default.law: Chapter VI-A as it applies to an HUF: ss.80C, 80D (premium for any member), 80G, 80TTA
default.plain: An HUF claims 80C, 80D, 80G and 80TTA. 80CCC, 80CCD, 80E, 80TTB and 80U are for individuals and are refused (the list is chip myreturn.rates via_status).

default.law: First Schedule Part I (age bands are for individuals)
default.plain: An HUF has no age: it always uses the below-60 slabs, whatever its date of formation.
An HUF never files ITR-1: ITR-2 without business, ITR-4 with presumptive business income, ITR-3 otherwise.
The return says status H, carries the date of formation where a person's birth date would be, and is verified by the Karta - the Karta's name, own PAN and father's name, capacity K.
The senior citizen's freedom from advance tax is for individuals; an HUF owes advance tax once it is over the threshold, so 234B / 234C apply.

default.law: s.115BAC (individuals, HUFs, AOPs, BOIs); First Schedule Part I
default.plain: Which regime a status is taxed under: individuals, HUFs, AOPs and BOIs choose new or old; a firm or LLP has its single rate.

default.law: First Schedule Part I (each status's rates); surcharge with marginal relief; cess
default.plain: The CA side's tax on total income for every status - slabs or flat rate, rebate where the status has it, surcharge with marginal relief, cess.
Slab tax and surcharge at one income; the tax rule asks it twice to work out marginal relief.

default.law: Finance Act 2025 rates; the export formats of the department's utility
default.plain: Every rate table the CA side uses, by status and by year (earlier years keep their own slabs and rebate).
House property from the books: 30% off a positive annual value; a loss counts only up to the set-off cap.
Interest on a refund: 0.5% a month from 1 April of the assessment year when filed by the due date, else from the filing date.

default.law: s.44AB (turnover / receipts limits; 44AD and 44ADA declared below the presumptive rate)
default.plain: Whether a tax audit is needed: business turnover above 1 crore (10 crore when cash receipts and payments are each within 5%), professional receipts above 50 lakh, or presumptive income declared lower than the presumptive rate with income above the basic exemption.
Only professional receipts make it a profession (the 50 lakh limit); any sales or services make it a business.
An LLP's accounts are audited unless turnover is within 40 lakh and contribution within 25 lakh; firms, AOPs and proprietors have no such audit.

default.law: CGST Act returns (GSTR-1, GSTR-3B) against the books
default.plain: The turnover in the books against the taxable value in GSTR-3B, and GSTR-3B against GSTR-1, for the year - a gap beyond the tolerance is a point for the audit.

default.law: ICAI announcement on Accounting Standards for non-company entities (from 1 April 2020)
default.plain: The entity's level (I to IV) by turnover, borrowings and listing - it decides which Accounting Standards apply in full.
The Form 3CD clauses that apply to this client, each shown only when its facts hold.

default.law: Finance Act 2026, First Schedule Part I-A Para E (AY 2026-27); ss.115BA, 115BAA, 115BAB; s.115JB(5A)
default.plain: A domestic company's rate from its option: normal provisions 25% when the total turnover or gross receipts of the PY 2023-24 did not exceed 400 crore, else 30% (a turnover not typed counts as above, and the screen says so); 115BA 25%; 115BAA 22%; 115BAB 15% on the manufacturing business and 22% on other income. Under 115BAA / 115BAB: a flat 10% surcharge, no MAT, no additional depreciation, only 80JJAA / 80M / 80LA(1A) of Chapter VI-A.
default.gaps: 115BAB's 15% is applied to the whole business income (the Act: income derived from or incidental to manufacturing); short-term gains on non-depreciable assets at 22% are not split out.

default.law: First Schedule Part I-A Paras E and F (surcharge, marginal relief); ss.111A, 112, 112A; Health and Education Cess; s.288B
default.plain: Tax on the total income: the option's rate on normal income, 20% on STCG u/s 111A, 12.5% on LTCG u/s 112A above 1.25 lakh and u/s 112; surcharge 7% above 1 crore and 12% above 10 crore with marginal relief (or a flat 10% under 115BAA / 115BAB); 4% cess; rounded to 10.
default.gaps: Marginal relief takes the income above the band's edge at the main rate (the usual case); a company whose special-rate gains straddle the edge should be checked by hand.

default.law: s.115JB (15% of book profit; Explanation 1 adjustments, Form 29B); s.115JAA (credit, 15 AYs); CBDT Circular 29/2019
default.plain: When the normal tax is below 15% of the book profit (with its own surcharge and cess), that MAT is the tax and the excess becomes a MAT credit; in a year the normal tax is higher, brought-forward credit is set off up to the difference, oldest first. No MAT and no credit under 115BAA / 115BAB. Book profit comes from rows tagged ITR6 MAT <item> (Form 29B); without them, from the P&L's profit before tax - and the screen says so.
default.gaps: Form 29B itself (the CA's report) is not produced; Ind AS transition adjustments (s.115JB(2A)-(2C)) are not worked out. The Finance Bill 2026's MAT changes (14%, MAT as final tax) apply from tax year 2026-27 under the Income-tax Act 2025, not to AY 2026-27.

default.law: s.32(1)(ii) and rule 5 / Appendix I; 2nd proviso to s.32(1) (under 180 days); s.32(1)(iia) and its 3rd proviso; s.50
default.plain: Each block from the fixed-asset schedule (rows tagged ITR6 DEP <block>): opening WDV + additions - sales; half rate on additions used under 180 days; additional 20% on new plant and machinery of a manufacturing company (half now, half next year); sales above the block are a short-term gain u/s 50.
default.gaps: Additional depreciation for the specified backward areas (35%, s.32(1)(iia) proviso), SLM for power units (s.32(1)(i)) and s.43(6)(c) adjustments for a block that ceases are not worked out.

default.plain: A brought-forward business loss is used only within 8 AYs, only when that year's return was in time, and - for a closely held company - only when 51% of the voting power stayed with the same holders; unabsorbed depreciation without limit; MAT credit within 15 AYs.
default.gaps: s.79(1)(b) (an eligible start-up whose original holders stay) and the s.79(2) exceptions (death, gift to a relative, amalgamation of a foreign company) are not taken; type s.79 as held when they apply.

default.plain: One loss against one income, never more than either: a house-property loss up to 2 lakh, a business loss against other heads (normal-rate income first), brought-forward business loss against business income only, unabsorbed depreciation against any head, short-term capital loss against any gain, long-term loss against long-term gains.

default.law: s.80G (incl. the 10% qualifying limit, s.80G(4)); proviso to s.80G(2)(iiihk)/(iiihl); s.115BAA(2)(ii)
default.plain: Donations without a limit at 100% / 50%; those within the qualifying limit together at most 10% of the adjusted gross total income; CSR contributions to the Swachh Bharat Kosh / Clean Ganga Fund get nothing; none under 115BAA / 115BAB.
default.gaps: Whether other CSR donations get 80G is contested; the category chosen on the row (ITR6 80G <category>) is the CA's call.

default.plain: Dividend received from another domestic company, a foreign company or a business trust is deducted up to the dividend the company itself distributed on or before one month prior to the due date of its return. Allowed under 115BAA / 115BAB too.
A company client's master data is checked: the CIN in the MCA's 21-character shape, 8-digit DINs, shareholdings 0-100% and not over 100% together, and 115BAB only for a manufacturing company.
Which document a figure is taken from when several give it (salary from Form 16, TDS from 26AS, other income from AIS ...). What the person types wins over every document.
Whether a figure agrees with another document (Form 16 TDS against 26AS, salary against AIS ...) - a gap is shown before filing.
How each document is recognised and read: Form 16, 26AS (text or PDF), AIS / TIS (JSON, CSV or PDF), the pre-filled JSON, a filed return, a bank statement (PDF, Excel, CSV).

When CBDT extends a due date by circular, interest under s.234A still runs from the original date if the tax owed after advance tax, TDS/TCS and reliefs is over one lakh; otherwise from the extended date. Circular 07/2026 is silent on interest, so the safer reading is used.
default.gaps: Ask a CA if the circular for a year says otherwise.

default.plain: Each transfer's gain is the sale less cost only, at 30%; a loss counts for nothing, is not set off even against another VDA's gain and is not carried forward.

default.law: Finance Act, First Schedule Part I (partial integration of agricultural income)
default.plain: Agricultural income over 5,000, when other income is above the basic exemption: tax on (normal + agricultural) less tax on (basic exemption + agricultural), in both regimes; 87A then applies.

Goods carriages, up to ten at any time: 1,000 per ton of gross weight per month for a vehicle over 12,000 kg, 7,500 per month for others; a part month counts as a month; higher income may be declared. More than ten vehicles: books, ITR-3.
80EEA is not allowed when 80EE is claimed: the return keeps 80EE and the check is red.

When the presumptive limits are passed, or the business is not presumptive, the profit typed from the person's own P&L is the income and the books flag is set; ITR-3 is written with the no-books P&L and balance sheet.
default.gaps: A business loss, depreciation and disallowances need a CA.

default.plain: Tax audit needed when business turnover is over 1 crore (10 crore with cash at 5% or less), professional receipts over 50 lakh (75 lakh), or presumptive income is declared lower than allowed with income above the basic exemption. My return then says: get a CA.

Holding periods (12 months listed, 24 months others), rates after 23 July 2024 (111A 20%, 112A 12.5% over 1.25 lakh, 112 12.5%), s.50AA debt funds and market-linked debentures always short-term at slab rates, and the set-off order: short-term loss against any gain, long-term loss only against long-term gain.

One sale's gain: price (or stamp value when over 110% of it), less cost, improvement and expenses; shares bought before 1 Feb 2018 use the higher of cost and the lower of the 31 Jan 2018 value and the price.
The cost inflation index from 2001-02 (100) to 2025-26 (376); an asset bought before 2001 uses its value on 1 April 2001.
Land or building bought before 23 July 2024 sold by a resident individual or HUF: tax at 12.5% without indexation or 20% with it, whichever is lower; both are shown.

54: house to house, cost up to 10 crore; 54EC: up to 50 lakh of bonds within six months; 54F: other asset to house in proportion, not with more than one other house; Capital Gains Account Scheme deposits count.
default.gaps: Time limits are not checked; one exemption per sale row.

default.plain: Losses net within each rate first, then a short-term loss against slab gains first and 112A last; a long-term loss against 112 before 112A.
Capital and house losses carry forward eight years; a capital loss only from a return filed on time; a brought-forward house loss is set off only against house income.

Gifts from relatives, on marriage, by will or inheritance are not taxed; money and valuables over 50,000 together in a year are; each property is tested on its own (stamp value, or shortfall over the higher of 50,000 and 10%).

Resident on 182 days, or 60 days and 365 in the four years before (182 for a citizen leaving for work or a visiting citizen/PIO; 120 when Indian income is over 15 lakh); deemed resident; RNOR by 9 of 10 years, 729 days in 7, the 120-day visitor and the deemed resident. A non-resident: no 87A, 80TTB, 80DD/DDB/U or senior limits; ITR-2/3 only.

For a resident and ordinarily resident: foreign income is taxed here, and relief per country and head is the lower of the tax paid abroad and the Indian tax at the average rate. Form 67 by 31 March of the assessment year.

default.law: Schedule FA; Black Money Act s.42-43
default.plain: A resident and ordinarily resident with any foreign asset or foreign income must list the assets in Schedule FA: red check otherwise.

A minor child's income (not from their own work or skill, nor a child with an 80U disability) is added to the parent's, less 1,500 per child; income from assets given to a spouse or son's wife without consideration is added under its head; Schedule SPI.
Salary arrears: tax this year with arrears less without, less the same difference for each earlier year at that year's slabs; never below nil; available in the new regime too.
default.gaps: An earlier year with surcharge is flagged, not relieved.

default.plain: An updated return within 48 months: not a loss or lower-tax return, not after search, survey or assessment; the further tax plus interest plus 25/50/60/70% by the year since.
default.gaps: No ITR-U JSON until its schema is added; 234C, surcharge and special rates of the earlier year are not computed.

params.label: each rule chip: area, law, plain sentence, what is not covered

description_nl: 2026-10-06 owner: the rule book a CA reviews - for each rule chip the section of the Act it follows, what it does in plain words and what it does not cover yet. Figures, worked examples and the chip's own wording are read from the rule chips by tools/rulebook.py, so the book cannot drift from the engine. 2026-10-07: 21 rules added (capital gains, residence and foreign income, clubbing, s.89, ITR-U, s.234A in an extended year, 44AE, agri, special rates). 2026-10-10: Schedule FA - every table A1-G is asked now (B a financial interest in an entity; D-F 2026-10-08), the gap note cleared. 2026-10-11: nine rules for a company's return (ITR-6): company.rate, company.tax, company.mat, company.dep_block, company.loss_ok, company.setoff, company.d80g, company.d80m, company.problem - each with what it does not cover yet.

The Form 3CD clauses that apply to this client, each shown only when its facts hold.

rules.law: Finance Act 2026, First Schedule Part I-A Para E (AY 2026-27); ss.115BA, 115BAA, 115BAB; s.115JB(5A)
rules.plain: A domestic company's rate from its option: normal provisions 25% when the total turnover or gross receipts of the PY 2023-24 did not exceed 400 crore, else 30% (a turnover not typed counts as above, and the screen says so); 115BA 25%; 115BAA 22%; 115BAB 15% on the manufacturing business and 22% on other income. Under 115BAA / 115BAB: a flat 10% surcharge, no MAT, no additional depreciation, only 80JJAA / 80M / 80LA(1A) of Chapter VI-A.
rules.gaps: 115BAB's 15% is applied to the whole business income (the Act: income derived from or incidental to manufacturing); short-term gains on non-depreciable assets at 22% are not split out.

rules.law: First Schedule Part I-A Paras E and F (surcharge, marginal relief); ss.111A, 112, 112A; Health and Education Cess; s.288B
rules.plain: Tax on the total income: the option's rate on normal income, 20% on STCG u/s 111A, 12.5% on LTCG u/s 112A above 1.25 lakh and u/s 112; surcharge 7% above 1 crore and 12% above 10 crore with marginal relief (or a flat 10% under 115BAA / 115BAB); 4% cess; rounded to 10.
rules.gaps: Marginal relief takes the income above the band's edge at the main rate (the usual case); a company whose special-rate gains straddle the edge should be checked by hand.

rules.law: s.115JB (15% of book profit; Explanation 1 adjustments, Form 29B); s.115JAA (credit, 15 AYs); CBDT Circular 29/2019
rules.plain: When the normal tax is below 15% of the book profit (with its own surcharge and cess), that MAT is the tax and the excess becomes a MAT credit; in a year the normal tax is higher, brought-forward credit is set off up to the difference, oldest first. No MAT and no credit under 115BAA / 115BAB. Book profit comes from rows tagged ITR6 MAT <item> (Form 29B); without them, from the P&L's profit before tax - and the screen says so.
rules.gaps: Form 29B itself (the CA's report) is not produced; Ind AS transition adjustments (s.115JB(2A)-(2C)) are not worked out. The Finance Bill 2026's MAT changes (14%, MAT as final tax) apply from tax year 2026-27 under the Income-tax Act 2025, not to AY 2026-27.

rules.law: s.32(1)(ii) and rule 5 / Appendix I; 2nd proviso to s.32(1) (under 180 days); s.32(1)(iia) and its 3rd proviso; s.50
rules.plain: Each block from the fixed-asset schedule (rows tagged ITR6 DEP <block>): opening WDV + additions - sales; half rate on additions used under 180 days; additional 20% on new plant and machinery of a manufacturing company (half now, half next year); sales above the block are a short-term gain u/s 50.
rules.gaps: Additional depreciation for the specified backward areas (35%, s.32(1)(iia) proviso), SLM for power units (s.32(1)(i)) and s.43(6)(c) adjustments for a block that ceases are not worked out.

rules.plain: A brought-forward business loss is used only within 8 AYs, only when that year's return was in time, and - for a closely held company - only when 51% of the voting power stayed with the same holders; unabsorbed depreciation without limit; MAT credit within 15 AYs.
rules.gaps: s.79(1)(b) (an eligible start-up whose original holders stay) and the s.79(2) exceptions (death, gift to a relative, amalgamation of a foreign company) are not taken; type s.79 as held when they apply.

rules.plain: One loss against one income, never more than either: a house-property loss up to 2 lakh, a business loss against other heads (normal-rate income first), brought-forward business loss against business income only, unabsorbed depreciation against any head, short-term capital loss against any gain, long-term loss against long-term gains.

rules.law: s.80G (incl. the 10% qualifying limit, s.80G(4)); proviso to s.80G(2)(iiihk)/(iiihl); s.115BAA(2)(ii)
rules.plain: Donations without a limit at 100% / 50%; those within the qualifying limit together at most 10% of the adjusted gross total income; CSR contributions to the Swachh Bharat Kosh / Clean Ganga Fund get nothing; none under 115BAA / 115BAB.
rules.gaps: Whether other CSR donations get 80G is contested; the category chosen on the row (ITR6 80G <category>) is the CA's call.

rules.plain: Dividend received from another domestic company, a foreign company or a business trust is deducted up to the dividend the company itself distributed on or before one month prior to the due date of its return. Allowed under 115BAA / 115BAB too.
A company client's master data is checked: the CIN in the MCA's 21-character shape, 8-digit DINs, shareholdings 0-100% and not over 100% together, and 115BAB only for a manufacturing company.
Which document a figure is taken from when several give it (salary from Form 16, TDS from 26AS, other income from AIS ...). What the person types wins over every document.
Whether a figure agrees with another document (Form 16 TDS against 26AS, salary against AIS ...) - a gap is shown before filing.
How each document is recognised and read: Form 16, 26AS (text or PDF), AIS / TIS (JSON, CSV or PDF), the pre-filled JSON, a filed return, a bank statement (PDF, Excel, CSV).

When CBDT extends a due date by circular, interest under s.234A still runs from the original date if the tax owed after advance tax, TDS/TCS and reliefs is over one lakh; otherwise from the extended date. Circular 07/2026 is silent on interest, so the safer reading is used.
rules.gaps: Ask a CA if the circular for a year says otherwise.

rules.plain: Each transfer's gain is the sale less cost only, at 30%; a loss counts for nothing, is not set off even against another VDA's gain and is not carried forward.

rules.law: Finance Act, First Schedule Part I (partial integration of agricultural income)
rules.plain: Agricultural income over 5,000, when other income is above the basic exemption: tax on (normal + agricultural) less tax on (basic exemption + agricultural), in both regimes; 87A then applies.

Goods carriages, up to ten at any time: 1,000 per ton of gross weight per month for a vehicle over 12,000 kg, 7,500 per month for others; a part month counts as a month; higher income may be declared. More than ten vehicles: books, ITR-3.
80EEA is not allowed when 80EE is claimed: the return keeps 80EE and the check is red.

When the presumptive limits are passed, or the business is not presumptive, the profit typed from the person's own P&L is the income and the books flag is set; ITR-3 is written with the no-books P&L and balance sheet.
rules.gaps: A business loss, depreciation and disallowances need a CA.

rules.plain: Tax audit needed when business turnover is over 1 crore (10 crore with cash at 5% or less), professional receipts over 50 lakh (75 lakh), or presumptive income is declared lower than allowed with income above the basic exemption. My return then says: get a CA.

Holding periods (12 months listed, 24 months others), rates after 23 July 2024 (111A 20%, 112A 12.5% over 1.25 lakh, 112 12.5%), s.50AA debt funds and market-linked debentures always short-term at slab rates, and the set-off order: short-term loss against any gain, long-term loss only against long-term gain.

One sale's gain: price (or stamp value when over 110% of it), less cost, improvement and expenses; shares bought before 1 Feb 2018 use the higher of cost and the lower of the 31 Jan 2018 value and the price.
The cost inflation index from 2001-02 (100) to 2025-26 (376); an asset bought before 2001 uses its value on 1 April 2001.
Land or building bought before 23 July 2024 sold by a resident individual or HUF: tax at 12.5% without indexation or 20% with it, whichever is lower; both are shown.

54: house to house, cost up to 10 crore; 54EC: up to 50 lakh of bonds within six months; 54F: other asset to house in proportion, not with more than one other house; Capital Gains Account Scheme deposits count.
rules.gaps: Time limits are not checked; one exemption per sale row.

rules.plain: Losses net within each rate first, then a short-term loss against slab gains first and 112A last; a long-term loss against 112 before 112A.
Capital and house losses carry forward eight years; a capital loss only from a return filed on time; a brought-forward house loss is set off only against house income.

Gifts from relatives, on marriage, by will or inheritance are not taxed; money and valuables over 50,000 together in a year are; each property is tested on its own (stamp value, or shortfall over the higher of 50,000 and 10%).

Resident on 182 days, or 60 days and 365 in the four years before (182 for a citizen leaving for work or a visiting citizen/PIO; 120 when Indian income is over 15 lakh); deemed resident; RNOR by 9 of 10 years, 729 days in 7, the 120-day visitor and the deemed resident. A non-resident: no 87A, 80TTB, 80DD/DDB/U or senior limits; ITR-2/3 only.

For a resident and ordinarily resident: foreign income is taxed here, and relief per country and head is the lower of the tax paid abroad and the Indian tax at the average rate. Form 67 by 31 March of the assessment year.

rules.law: Schedule FA; Black Money Act s.42-43
rules.plain: A resident and ordinarily resident with any foreign asset or foreign income must list the assets in Schedule FA: red check otherwise.

A minor child's income (not from their own work or skill, nor a child with an 80U disability) is added to the parent's, less 1,500 per child; income from assets given to a spouse or son's wife without consideration is added under its head; Schedule SPI.
Salary arrears: tax this year with arrears less without, less the same difference for each earlier year at that year's slabs; never below nil; available in the new regime too.
rules.gaps: An earlier year with surcharge is flagged, not relieved.

rules.plain: An updated return within 48 months: not a loss or lower-tax return, not after search, survey or assessment; the further tax plus interest plus 25/50/60/70% by the year since.
rules.gaps: No ITR-U JSON until its schema is added; 234C, surcharge and special rates of the earlier year are not computed.
